    AI Overview
    The Artemis II Orion capsule successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10, 2026. This safe, parachute-assisted "textbook touchdown" marked the end of a historic 10-day mission, with the crew of four in good health and the capsule successfully retrieved by Navy teams. 
    • Final Moments: The capsule hit the water at approximately 20 mph, with five orange airbags activating to flip it upright.
    • Mission Significance: This flight is the first crewed, deep-space journey of the Artemis program, designed to test equipment for future lunar surface landings.
    • Next Steps: The crew is set to be extracted from the capsule by Amentum recovery teams to return to the Navy vessel, paving the way for future Artemis missions.
